questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why concert tickets are so expensive
How blind and deaf people enjoy art galleries and concerts
The history of the harp in Britain
How new instruments help disabled musicians make music
questions.why: They hear from a composer whose work with “new instruments” allows disabled musicians to express themselves.

questions.q: What did the UK's Equality Act of 2010 do?
options: Gave disabled people equal access to education, work and arts
Gave free concert tickets to disabled people
Required every theatre to be rebuilt
Created lots of new music schools just for disabled children in the UK
questions.why: Neil says it guaranteed disabled people's rights to equal access to education, employment and services.

questions.q: What did the study by Attitude is Everything find?
options: Most venues were fully accessible
Disabled musicians now earn much more money than other musicians
A third of music venues gave no disabled access information
Half of all concerts were cancelled
questions.why: It found one third of music venues provided no disabled access information at all.

options: A harpist who is dyslexic
A composer who writes music for new instruments
The manager of the Royal Albert Hall concert venue in London
A campaigner for the Equality Act
questions.why: She's a music composer who composes music to be played by “new instruments”.

questions.q: According to Megan, how can a new instrument be made?
options: Only by large factories
By a factory, or by the musician themselves
Only by music colleges
Only from traditional materials like wood and metal
questions.why: She says they may be mass-produced or designed and built by the musician themselves.

questions.q: What is special about the Rainbow Harp?
options: It has no strings at all
It is played with the feet instead of the hands and fingers
It can only play one note
Its strings are coloured, and each colour is a different note
questions.why: Megan says it has colour-coded strings, and each colour corresponds to a different pitch.

questions.q: Why did Morwenna and her husband create the Rainbow Harp?
options: Dyslexia made black and white music notation hard for her
She wanted to sell harps to schools
Traditional harps were far too big and heavy for her to carry
Her teacher asked her to invent an instrument
questions.why: Morwenna is dyslexic and found traditional black and white notation an obstacle.

questions.q: Why does Georgie mention Morwenna's harp teacher?
options: To show that the teacher designed the harp
To explain why Morwenna stopped playing music for many years
To explain what led to the Rainbow Harp being invented
To praise traditional teaching methods
questions.why: When the teacher wanted her to read sheet music her brain froze, “and that's how the Rainbow Harp was invented”.
